story_beats.title: A CHARGE IS NOT A FINDING
story_beats.line: The filing mixes a supposed missing girl with a disputed property claim after confused wedding arrangements. Its missing-person story is an allegation: the complaint lacks a verified identity, residence, and firsthand account. Keep the reported property out of the same evidentiary column until its owner, chain, and record are shown.
choices: Record the office discussion as directly heard
Keep the missing-person story in the allegation column
Require an identified witness and itemized property record
choice_responses: The conflicting arrangements were heard in the office; that does not prove a girl or property was taken.
A repeated charge stays an allegation until reliable evidence supports it.
Without a named witness and traceable property record, the filing cannot stand as a finding.
story_beats.response: Procedure starts with particulars, not a verdict. The confused report and property claim remain contested.

story_beats.title: SORT THE EVIDENCE, NOT THE PEOPLE
story_beats.line: Keep four entries distinct: what a witness directly observed; what was heard from someone else; testimony shaped by payment, threats, or coaching; and claims invented to fill a gap. Polishetty says the supposed wall-crossing was not something he saw and describes pressure to repeat a story. Gavarayya refuses to pass an invented spirit claim off as proof. None of those compromised accounts establishes the charge.
choices: File only a witness's own sight or hearing as direct observation
Mark a report repeated from another person as hearsay
Flag payment, threats, or a coached script as compromised testimony
Set aside an invented claim as fabrication, not corroboration
choice_responses: Direct observation belongs in its own row, with the witness and circumstances identified.
Hearsay records what was repeated, not what the witness personally saw.
Bribed or coached testimony is evidence of pressure on the process, not proof of the allegation.
A fabricated claim cannot corroborate another claim merely by being repeated.
story_beats.response: A statement is not reliable because it is written down. The record must preserve how each account was obtained.

story_beats.title: DO NOT MERGE THE FAMILY FILES
story_beats.line: Agnihotravadhani's separate marriage bargain concerns his daughter Subbi. Lubdhavadhani's regret concerns selling his own daughter Meenakshi in marriage to an older man. Those are distinct family matters, not explanations for the missing-person claim. Neither daughter is a clue, prize, obstacle, or mission object in this case.
choices: Keep Agnihotravadhani's bargain over Subbi in its own record
Keep Lubdhavadhani's regret about Meenakshi separate
Do not turn either daughter into evidence or an objective
choice_responses: Subbi's separate marriage bargain cannot identify the person named in the complaint.
Meenakshi's father's regret is not testimony about the disputed missing-person case.
A daughter is not a clue, prize, or obstacle to be moved by this case file.
story_beats.response: The records stay separate: Subbi's bargain, Meenakshi's father's regret, and the missing-person allegation are not interchangeable.

story_beats.title: IDENTITY, WITHOUT SPECTACLE
story_beats.line: Madhuravani gives a voluntary, uncoached account: the supposed missing girl and bride is Karataka Śāstri's male disciple in disguise. The disciple is not Meenakshi or Buchchamma. This is a person misidentified by the dispute, not a punchline, mission object, prize, or obstacle. Record the identity without exposing a private location; keep the disputed property claim on its own evidentiary track.
choices: Take Madhuravani's account voluntarily and without public exposure
Record Karataka Śāstri's disciple as the person identified
Keep the property claim separate from the identity finding
choice_responses: Madhuravani's account is recorded on her terms, without a forced or rehearsed statement.
The person sought is the male disciple in disguise, not Meenakshi or Buchchamma.
An identity disclosure does not establish who owned or moved the disputed property.
story_beats.response: The firsthand identification resolves who the supposed missing bride is. It does not turn the separate property claim into proof.

story_beats.title: BUCCHAMMA'S FUTURE IS HERS
story_beats.line: Sowjanya recognizes that Madhuravani protected the disciple and gave an honest account. She rejects Gireesam's self-serving claim to reform and tells him to stay away from Buchchamma's future. Sowjanya supports Buchchamma's education and independence: Buchchamma will choose for herself whether, when, and whom to marry. The three women discuss their next steps; the scene ends on their agency, not Gireesam.
choices: Record Sowjanya's recognition of Madhuravani's protection
Respect Sowjanya's refusal of Gireesam's approach
Back Buchchamma's education and self-chosen future
choice_responses: Madhuravani's protection is acknowledged without trading it for a reward or a private bargain.
Gireesam does not earn access to Buchchamma through charm, deception, or a claim of reform.
Buchchamma's education and independent future belong to Buchchamma to decide.
story_beats.response: The inquiry closes as unsupported on this episode's evidence, not as an invented historical decree. Madhuravani, Sowjanya, and Buchchamma leave with Buchchamma's education and future in her own hands.
